title: Sylvester–Frobenius via Mathlib's Canonical Predicate (Chicken McNugget)
description: The two-coin Sylvester–Frobenius / Chicken McNugget theorem $g(m, n) = mn - m - n$ for coprime $m, n > 1$, stated with Mathlib's **canonical** `FrobeniusNumber` predicate $\text{FrobeniusNumber}\,k\,s := \text{IsGreatest}\,\{j \mid j \notin \text{AddSubmonoid.closure}\,s\}\,k$ rather than the homemade `Representable` predicate of the gallery's parent entry `Proofs/FrobeniusNumber.lean`. Invokes `frobeniusNumber_pair` and unpacks it via `frobeniusNumber_iff` (the bare not-in-closure / above-in-closure split) and via `AddSubmonoid.mem_closure_pair` (the elementary form $\exists a\,b,\ am + bn = k$). The Chicken McNugget instance $g(3, 5) = 7$ is the canonical `FrobeniusNumber 7 {3,5}` with its fully elementary unpacking ($\neg\exists a\,b,\ 3a + 5b = 7$ and $\forall k > 7,\ \exists a\,b,\ 3a + 5b = k$). 9 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

mathlibDependencies.description: The Chicken McNugget theorem: for coprime m, n > 1, `FrobeniusNumber (m*n - m - n) {m, n}`, i.e. m*n - m - n is the greatest natural number not in the additive submonoid generated by {m, n}. The single deep ingredient; everything in this entry is an unpacking of it.
`FrobeniusNumber n s ↔ n ∉ AddSubmonoid.closure s ∧ ∀ k > n, k ∈ AddSubmonoid.closure s`. Used to split the canonical IsGreatest claim into the not-representable / above-representable pair.

`c ∈ AddSubmonoid.closure {a, b} ↔ ∃ m n : ℕ, m • a + n • b = c`. Combined with `smul_eq_mul` over ℕ, this is the elementary bridge turning closure-membership into the representability statement `∃ a b, a*m + b*n = k`.

overview.historicalContext: The Frobenius coin problem asks for the largest integer not expressible as a nonnegative combination of given coprime denominations. The two-generator case was solved by J.J. Sylvester in 1884 with the closed form $g(m, n) = mn - m - n$; it is popularly known as the Chicken McNugget theorem (the largest number of McNuggets one cannot buy in boxes of two coprime sizes). The gallery's parent entry `Proofs/FrobeniusNumber.lean` proves this with a hand-rolled representability predicate `Representable a b n := ∃ x y, n = a*x + b*y` and a plain function `frobeniusNumber a b := a*b - a - b`, encoding the 'largest non-representable' claim by hand across several lemmas. Mathlib instead packages the entire notion canonically: `FrobeniusNumber n s := IsGreatest { k | k ∉ AddSubmonoid.closure s } n`, where `AddSubmonoid.closure {m, n}` is the verified general notion of 'nonnegative integer combination' and `IsGreatest` captures both 'not representable' and 'greatest such' in one structure. This entry restates Sylvester–Frobenius on that canonical footing.
overview.problemStatement: For coprime $m, n > 1$, prove $\text{FrobeniusNumber}(mn - m - n, \{m, n\})$ — i.e. $mn - m - n$ is the greatest natural number not lying in $\text{AddSubmonoid.closure}\,\{m, n\}$ — and unpack it into the elementary statements that $mn - m - n$ is not of the form $am + bn$ while every larger integer is. Instantiate the Chicken McNugget case $g(3, 5) = 7$.
overview.proofStrategy: Part I builds the elementary bridge `mem_closure_pair_iff`: membership in `AddSubmonoid.closure {m, n}` is exactly `∃ a b : ℕ, a*m + b*n = k`, obtained from `AddSubmonoid.mem_closure_pair` by rewriting the ℕ-scalar action `•` to `*` via `smul_eq_mul`. Part II re-exports `frobeniusNumber_pair` as `sylvester_frobenius_canonical` and splits it with `frobeniusNumber_iff` into `frobenius_not_in_closure` and `above_frobenius_in_closure`. Part III composes Parts I and II to land the fully elementary corollaries `frobenius_not_representable` (¬∃ a b, a*m + b*n = m*n - m - n) and `above_frobenius_representable` (∀ k > m*n - m - n, ∃ a b, a*m + b*n = k). Part IV instantiates m = 3, n = 5: after rewriting 7 = 3*5 - 3 - 5 (norm_num) and discharging `Nat.Coprime 3 5` by `decide`, the McNugget facts `mcnugget_canonical`, `seven_not_representable`, and `above_seven_representable` follow.
keyInsights: The value of this entry over the parent `FrobeniusNumber.lean` is **provenance**, not new arithmetic: by grounding the theorem in `AddSubmonoid.closure` and `IsGreatest`, the 'largest non-representable' claim is no longer encoded by a hand-rolled predicate but inherited verbatim from Mathlib's verified development. The homemade `Representable` predicate and the canonical closure-membership are then shown to coincide (`mem_closure_pair_iff`), so the elementary corollaries read in the same `a*m + b*n` language while every step is machine-checked against the general theory.

`AddSubmonoid.mem_closure_pair` is the precise hinge that connects abstract submonoid membership to elementary representability. Over ℕ the additive `ℕ`-action `n • x` is just `n * x` (`smul_eq_mul`), so `∃ m n, m • a + n • b = c` collapses to `∃ a b, a*m + b*n = k` with a single `simp only`.

Splitting the canonical `IsGreatest`/`FrobeniusNumber` predicate with `frobeniusNumber_iff` cleanly separates the two halves of Sylvester's theorem — non-representability of the extremal value and representability of everything above it — each of which is independently useful and each of which transfers to the elementary `a*m + b*n` language via the Part I bridge.

The Chicken McNugget instance uses `decide` (kernel reduction) rather than `native_decide` for `Nat.Coprime 3 5`, keeping the entry genuinely axiom-free: `#print axioms` reports only `propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`, none of which is a mathematical assumption (in particular `Lean.ofReduceBool` does not appear).

conclusion.summary: Restates the two-coin Sylvester–Frobenius / Chicken McNugget theorem $g(m, n) = mn - m - n$ for coprime $m, n > 1$ on Mathlib's canonical footing — the `FrobeniusNumber` predicate built from `IsGreatest` and `AddSubmonoid.closure` — and bridges it back to the elementary representability language $\exists a\,b,\ am + bn = k$ via `AddSubmonoid.mem_closure_pair`. Includes the Chicken McNugget instance $g(3, 5) = 7$ in both canonical and elementary form. 9 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: By deriving the elementary corollaries from Mathlib's verified `frobeniusNumber_pair` rather than a homemade predicate, this entry shows that the gallery's hand-rolled two-coin development (`Proofs/FrobeniusNumber.lean`) agrees with the canonical theory, and provides a drop-in canonical statement for downstream work that prefers `AddSubmonoid.closure` over the bespoke `Representable`. The pattern — invoke the packaged theorem, split with its `_iff`, then translate closure-membership to a concrete combination — is reusable for any numerical-semigroup result stated against `AddSubmonoid.closure`.
openQuestions: The three-or-more-generator Frobenius number has no closed form (NP-hard in general); the canonical `FrobeniusNumber` predicate over an arbitrary finite set `s` is the right vehicle for stating the partial results that do exist (arithmetic-progression and special-family formulas), paralleling the homemade three-generator development in `frobenius-number-oq-03`.

Can the homemade `Representable`/`frobeniusNumber` API of the parent entry be retired in favor of the canonical `AddSubmonoid.closure`/`FrobeniusNumber` formulation throughout the family, with `mem_closure_pair_iff` as the single translation lemma?
